\"test_file\": test_file,\n+                \"test_functions\": quality[\"test_functions\"],\n+                \"loc_weight\": loc_weight,\n+            },\n+        }\n+    if quality_kind == \"placeholder_smoke\":\n+        return {\n+            \"file\": prod_file,\n+            \"name\": f\"placeholder::{basename}\",\n+            \"tier\": 2,\n+            \"confidence\": \"high\",\n+     },\n+        }\n+    if quality_kind == \"snapshot_heavy\":\n+        return {\n+            \"file\": prod_file,\n+            \"name\": f\"snapshot_heavy::{basename}\",\n+            \"tier\": > AGENT

> AGENT

Yes. It was triggered during my run, and I traced why.

Cause:
- Your live plan file [plan.json](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/.desloppify/plan.json) got written with triage fixture data (`queue_order = triage::observe/reflect/organize/commit`).
- The `triage_stages` reports in that file exactly match the test fixture text used in triage tests (the “A sufficiently long report for the stage...” string), so this came from test side effects, not from `desloppify next` itself.
- I ran triage command tests while refactoring triage wiring; those tests monkeypatch `load_plan` to in-memory plans, and in some paths `save_plan` still wrote that plan to the real `.desloppify/plan.json`.

So the jump happened because plan state was polluted into “TRIAGE MODE (3/4 complete)”, which put `triage::commit` at the top of the queue.

If you want, I’ll now clean this safely and continue the queue from the intended next issue.

None:\n    \"\"\"Return passthrough call target when stmt is `return target(...)`.\"\"\"\n    if not isinstance(stmt, ast.Return):\n        return None\n    value = stmt.value\n    if not isinstance(value, ast.Call):\n        return None\n    target = value.func\n    if isinstance(target, ast.Name):\n        return target.id\n    return None\n\n\ndef _find_python_passthrough_wrappers(tree: ast.Module) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:\n    \"\"\"Find Python wrapper pairs via AST traversal.\"\"\"\n    wrappers: list[tuple[str, str]] = []\n    for node in ast.walk(tree):\n        if not isinstance(node, ast.FunctionDef | ast.AsyncFunctionDef):\n            continue\n\n        body = _strip_docstring(list(node.body))\n        if len(body) != 1:\n            continue\n\n        target_name = _python_passthrough_target(body[0])\n        if target_name and node.name != target_name:\n            wrappers.append((node.name, target_name))\n    return wrappers\n\n\ndef _is_delegation_stmt(stmt: ast.stmt) -> str | None:\n    \"\"\"Return delegate attribute when *stmt* is a pure delegation call/access.\"\"\"\n    if isinstance(stmt, ast.Expr):\n        value = stmt.value\n    elif isinstance(stmt, ast.Return) and stmt.value is not None:\n        value = stmt.value\n    else:\n        return None\n\n    if isinstance(value, ast.Call):\n        value = value.func\n\n    node = value\n    depth = 0\n    while isinstance(node, ast.Attribute):\n        node = node.value\n        depth += 1\n    if depth < 1 or not isinstance(node, ast.Name) or node.id != \"self\":\n        return None\n\n    first = value\n    while isinstance(first, ast.Attribute) and isinstance(first.value, ast.Attribute):\n        first = first.value\n    if isinstance(first, ast.Attribute) and isinstance(first.value, ast.Name):\n        return first.attr\n    return None\n\n\ndef _find_delegation_heavy_classes(tree: ast.Module) -> list[dict]:\n    \"\"\"Find classes where most methods delegate to a single inner object.\"\"\"\n    results: list[dict] = []\n    for node in ast.walk(tree):\n        if not isinstance(node, ast.ClassDef):\n            continue\n\n        methods: list[ast.FunctionDef | ast.AsyncFunctionDef] = [\n            child\n            for child in node.body\n            if isinstance(child, ast.FunctionDef | ast.AsyncFunctionDef)\n            and child.name != \"__init__\"\n        ]\n        if len(methods) <= 3:\n            continue\n\n        delegating_methods: dict[str, list[str]] = {}\n        for method in methods:\n            body = _strip_docstring(list(method.body))\n            if len(body) != 1:\n                continue\n            attr = _is_delegation_stmt(body[0])\n            if attr:\n                delegating_methods.setdefault(attr, []).append(method.name)\n\n        if not delegating_methods:\n            continue\n\n        top_attr = max(delegating_methods, key=lambda a: len(delegating_methods[a]))\n        delegate_count = len(delegating_methods[top_attr])\n        ratio = delegate_count / len(methods)\n        if ratio > 0.5:\n            results.append(\n                {\n                    \"class_name\": node.name,\n                    \"line\": node.lineno,\n                    \"delegation_ratio\": round(ratio, 2),\n                    \"method_count\": len(methods),\n                    \"delegate_count\": delegate_count,\n                    \"delegate_target\": top_attr,\n                    \"sample_methods\": delegating_methods[top_attr][:5],\n                }\n            )\n    return results\n\n\ndef _find_facade_modules(tree: ast.Module, *, loc: int) -> dict | None:\n    \"\"\"Detect modules where >70% of public names come from imports.\"\"\"\n    import_names: set[str] = set()\n    defined_names: set[str] = set()\n\n    for node in ast.iter_child_nodes(tree):\n        if isinstance(node, ast.Import):\n            for alias in node.names:\n                name = alias.asname or alias.name.split(\".\")[-1]\n                import_names.add(name)\n        elif isinstance(node, ast.ImportFrom):\n            for alias in node.names:\n                if alias.name == \"*\":\n                    continue\n                name = alias.asname or alias.name\n                import_names.add(name)\n        elif isinstance(node, ast.FunctionDef | ast.AsyncFunctionDef):\n            defined_names.add(node.name)\n        elif isinstance(node, ast.ClassDef):\n            defined_names.add(node.name)\n        elif isinstance(node, ast.Assign):\n            for target in node.targets:\n                if isinstance(target, ast.Name) and target.id == \"__all__\":\n                    continue\n                if isinstance(target, ast.Name):\n                    defined_names.add(target.id)\n\n    public_imports = {n for n in import_names if not n.startswith(\"_\")}\n    public_defs = {n for n in defined_names if not n.startswith(\"_\")}\n\n    total_public = len(public_imports | public_defs)\n    if total_public < 3:\n        return None\n\n    re_exported = public_imports - public_defs\n    re_export_ratio = len(re_exported) / total_public\n\n    if re_export_ratio < 0.7 or len(public_defs) > 3:\n        return None\n\n    return {\n        \"re_export_ratio\": round(re_export_ratio, 2),\n        \"defined_symbols\": len(public_defs),\n        \"re_exported_symbols\": len(re_exported),\n        \"samples\": sorted(re_exported)[:5],\n        \"loc\": loc,\n    }\n\n\n__all__ = [\n    \"_find_delegation_heavy_classes\",\n    \"_find_facade_modules\",\n    \"_find_python_passthrough_wrappers\",\n    \"_is_delegation_stmt\",\n    \"_python_passthrough_target\",\n]\nPY",

Of the current `406` queued items, the ones that are genuinely bad engineering (not just ugly) are:

1. Queue/state integrity drift (process bug)
- `7` queue IDs point to files that no longer exist (`desloppify/app/commands/fix/apply_flow.py`, `desloppify/app/commands/_fix_preview.py`, `desloppify/languages/python/_review.py`).
- That is engineering-bad because triage is now partially targeting dead paths while the real code moved to [apply_flow.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/autofix/apply_flow.py), [preview.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/autofix/preview.py), and [review.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/languages/python/review.py).

2. Incomplete migration / private API coupling
- `review::.::holistic::incomplete_migration::...::63d229a7` is real architectural debt.
- The triage split still depends on transitional private wiring across modules like [triage_handlers.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/plan/triage_handlers.py) and [confirmations.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/plan/triage/confirmations.py), which is fragile and hard to evolve safely.

3. Real security-risk item: shell execution path
- `security::...B602...unused.py::230` at [unused.py:230](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/languages/typescript/detectors/unused.py:230) (`shell=(sys.platform == "win32")`).
- This is the security finding I’d treat as materially important.

4. Shared mutable global state
- `global_mutable_config::...base/registry.py::DETECTORS` at [registry.py:402](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/base/registry.py:402) (plus related globals).
- This is a real reliability risk (order-dependent behavior, test bleed, plugin side effects).

5. High-complexity critical code without direct tests
- `test_coverage::...status/cmd.py::untested_critical` for [cmd.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/status/cmd.py).
- `orphaned::...base/discovery/scan.py` for [scan.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/base/discovery/scan.py).
- These are real correctness/maintainability risks, not cosmetic.

Mostly ugly (lower urgency):
- Most `structural`, `smells`, and `responsibility_cohesion` items are maintainability debt.
- Most `B324` (`md5`) items are fingerprinting/dup-detection style uses, not auth/crypto boundary failures.

> DEVELOPER

And does that align with this:                                                                                                                                   
  Tier 1: Actual bugs / correctness risks                                                                                       

  1. Import cycle (1 issue) — schema.py ↔ schema_scores.py. This is a real architectural defect that can cause subtle import-time
  failures or None references. Already reopened once (prior fix was reverted).
  2. Schema drift (3 issues) — Dict literals using inconsistent keys (initial_review, primary_command, recurring_dims). These are
  data correctness bugs — one place constructs a dict with the wrong key, and downstream code looking for the standard key
  silently gets None. High priority.
  3. Silent except / swallowed errors (4 issues) — runner_parallel.py catches exceptions with pass/continue. This hides real
  failures during review runs. You won't know when things break.
  4. Monster functions (9 issues) — Functions >150 LOC. The ones in execution.py, display.py, and the parser groups are real
  maintainability hazards — hard to test, hard to reason about, easy to introduce bugs when modifying.
  5. Noop functions (8 issues) — Non-trivial functions whose body does nothing. These are dead code that looks alive — someone
  will waste time trying to understand or extend them. Quick wins to delete.
  6. Unused imports (45 issues) — Most are re-exports in runner_parallel.py (8 private re-exports that nothing uses). The
  WORKFLOW_CREATE_PLAN_ID and purge_ids in plan/cmd.py suggest dead code paths. Easy cleanup, removes confusion.

  Tier 2: Real design debt

  7. Global mutable config (11 issues) — Module-level mutable dicts/lists modified from multiple sites (DETECTORS, _registry,
  _flags, _load_errors). This is a real testability and concurrency hazard. Not urgent but genuinely bad engineering — makes the
  system harder to reason about and test in isolation.
  8. High cyclomatic complexity (33 issues) — Functions with too many branches. These are the functions where bugs hide.
  Prioritize the ones in engine/detection code over CLI rendering code.
  9. Test coverage gaps (60 issues) — Some are real risks:
    - status/cmd.py: "untested critical module, high blast radius" — 270 LOC with 0 importers and no tests
    - scan.py: untested 117 LOC module
    - The ~50 "transitive only" issues are lower priority (code is exercised, just not directly tested)
  10. Private cross-module imports (46 issues) — Modules importing _private functions from other modules. This breaks
  encapsulation and makes refactoring dangerous. The triage/display.py importing 5 private helpers from helpers/display.py is the
  worst offender — these should be made public or the modules should be restructured.

  ---
